name: Forward lunge
summary: Step forward and lower until both knees are at about 90°, then push back to standing.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working leg nearest. Step that foot forward and lower straight down until the front thigh is level and the back knee hovers above the floor. Push off the front foot to return.
brief: Stand tall. Step the working foot forward and lower straight down until the front thigh is level and the back knee hovers above the floor.
why: From the side the front knee angle gives depth, and the trunk pitching forward — the usual cheat — shows as the shoulder–hip line tilting.
regression: Split squat with no step; shorter step.
contraindications: Kneecap pain on the front leg; balance problems.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Knee dropping inward
faults.tip: The front knee tracks over the foot. Inward collapse is the commonest lunge fault.

faults.label: Front knee shooting past the toes
faults.tip: Take a longer step so the shin stays close to upright; the knee should stay over the foot.

faults.label: Step too short
faults.tip: A short step drives the knee far past the toes and loads the kneecap.

faults.label: Not lowering enough
faults.tip: Drop the back knee toward the floor; the front thigh should reach level.

faults.label: Front heel lifting
faults.tip: Drive up through the front heel; if it lifts, the stride is too short or the weight is on the toes.

guide.surface: Enough floor for a long step.

points.t: Thigh reaches level; shin near vertical.
